artifacts.summary: Finds leanprover/lean-action@v1 already caches .lake/build via its built-in GitHub Actions cache (confirmed live in run logs and the repo's cache store); recommends dropping deliverable (a) as filed and keeping only the ci.yml timeout-minutes parity fix (b).

claim_invalidations.claim: The task's filed premise that '.lake/build' has NO build cache in any CI workflow (and that the project's own build artifacts are discarded between runs) is refuted for FormalSystem/Mathlib: leanprover/lean-action@v1, used by ci.yml/docs.yml/release.yml, defaults use-github-cache to true and already caches the whole .lake directory via its own actions/cache/restore+save steps, confirmed live via a run log cache-hit/restore and 4 real cache entries in this repository's Actions cache store.

memory_candidates.content: leanprover/lean-action@v1 (the composite action used for `lake build`/test/lint in CI) has a built-in GitHub Actions cache of the whole .lake directory, controlled by a `use-github-cache` input that defaults to true. It restores/saves via actions/cache keyed on runner os/arch + lean-toolchain hash + lake-manifest.json hash + commit sha, with a sha-less restore-keys fallback for incremental cross-commit restores. The save happens inside that one composite step, so any lake build invoked in a LATER step of the same job is not covered by it. Before concluding a Lean project's CI has no build-artifact cache from a grep of the workflow YAML alone, check whether leanprover/lean-action (or any composite action) is already doing it internally -- verify with `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/actions/caches` and a run log grep for 'Cache restored from key'.
